summary: Iteration 25 e2e testing of Prize League Phase-2 sprint. Backend: 23/25 pytests pass (Engines 2 & 3, Image processor, User 360 GET, Erase RBAC all green). 2 failures on suspend/unsuspend endpoints are traced to a route-registration ordering bug (admin_routes.py registers /api/admin/users/{user_id}/suspend + /unsuspend BEFORE user360_routes.py, so the new password-gated + audit-logged handlers in user360_routes are UNREACHABLE — FastAPI serves the older no-op handlers instead). Frontend: user-360-page renders with all required data-testids; user-link navigation works; suspend dialog opens with reason+password fields and closes on cancel. EditContestDialog upload calls POST /api/admin/uploads/contest-image and populates both form.image (card.jpg) and form.mobile_image (mobile.jpg). Image processor produces exactly 5 variants at correct dimensions (300x200/600x400/900x600/1600x900/2000x1500), each URL is HTTP 200 and has no EXIF. Non-image upload correctly returns 415. iter22 regression suite 14/14 green.

critical.issue: Route collision: admin_routes.py registers these routes (no password re-auth, no audit_log write) BEFORE user360_routes.py in server.py. FastAPI resolves to the FIRST registered path, so the new user360 handlers (which require admin_password + write audit_log kind='user_suspend'/'user_unsuspend') are dead code. Impact: (1) any admin can suspend any user WITHOUT re-entering their password (RBAC weakness) — during our test the super admin himself was suspended by a request that sent 'admin_password: WRONG_PASSWORD' and got 200; (2) no user_suspend/user_unsuspend audit rows are ever created; (3) the reason field from the UI is silently dropped. Fix: delete or rename the legacy handlers at admin_routes.py:96 & :105, OR move app.include_router(user360_router) above app.include_router(admin_router) in server.py.

issues: React warning: 'Missing Description or aria-describedby={undefined} for DialogContent' on both confirm dialogs — accessibility polish, add DialogDescription.

action_items: CRITICAL: Remove or shadow the legacy suspend/unsuspend handlers in /app/backend/routers/admin_routes.py (lines 96 & 105). They shadow the new secure endpoints in user360_routes.py. critical_code_review_comments: Route collision above is a security regression in admin flow. Also note admin_routes suspend endpoint does not check admin_password at all — any admin/support/operator role can suspend any user.

user360_routes.py:143-160 erase_user: masks email but does NOT null-out picture in some code paths and does not scrub wallet PII; retention of financial history is by design but consider explicit comment. Also uses email comparison for self-erase — could switch to user_id comparison to be robust against email-mutation.

engines_routes.py:267 reveal_instant_win is mounted under /api/admin (Super-Admin router prefix). The docstring says 'Called by the frontend AFTER a user completes the required skill task' — but the endpoint requires admin role via require_admin? No — actually it uses get_current_user (not require_admin). However it lives under /api/admin/engines/instant-win/*, which is fine for RBAC-agnostic access but is a confusing URL for a player-facing endpoint. Consider mounting reveal on /api/engines/instant-win/{contest_id}/reveal for clarity.

uploads_routes.py contest-image: focal_x/focal_y are only clamped, not validated as floats — a malformed value like 'abc' will throw a raw ValueError → HTTP 500 instead of 422. Wrap the float() cast in a try/except and raise HTTPException(422).
user360_routes.py DeleteRequest is reused for suspend (which requires admin_password + reason) but the model does not distinguish required-vs-optional per operation. Acceptable for now.

rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: New endpoints in user360_routes.py duplicate paths that already existed in admin_routes.py. FastAPI does not raise on duplicate registration; it matches routes in registration order. server.py registers admin_router at line 86 and user360_router at line 112 (26 routers later). All /api/admin/users/{user_id}/suspend and /unsuspend requests therefore route to the legacy handlers, bypassing password re-auth and audit_log emission. REPRODUCTION: (1) login as super admin, get JWT; (2) POST /api/admin/users/<victim>/suspend body={'reason':'x','admin_password':'WRONG'}; (3) response is 200 and the user is suspended in DB despite password mismatch; (4) no audit_log doc with kind='user_suspend' is written. MITIGATION: delete lines 96-102 and 105-111 of admin_routes.py (they are the older stub), OR move `app.include_router(user360_router)` above `app.include_router(admin_router)` in server.py. Verified restoration: after test we manually flipped users.suspended=false for bachanta8@gmail.com so admin login is not blocked.
